**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve recipe-less VPATH providers in runtime group inputs**

When a VPATH prerequisite has an explicit recipe-less rule, this replacement never runs because the child has a rule and retains its lexical output name. For example, with `VPATH := sources`, an existing `sources/input`, `input:`, and `output:: input` whose recipe is `cat $< > $@`, generated execution passes `input` rather than `sources/input` and fails when creating the missing output. `src/ninja.cc` deliberately emits these source aliases without materializing a local file, while the previous generation-time expansion used `EffectivePrerequisite()` to recover their provider. Serialize that provider mapping for runtime automatic variables and group freshness as well; handling only unruled VPATH inputs leaves this supported case broken.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match lexical group prerequisites to their logical metadata**

For a prerequisite spelled with parent-directory components, group inputs retain the lexical name while `MakeRuntimeRecipe()` serializes phony/logical metadata using canonical `node.deps` keys. These exact-symbol lookups therefore miss the prerequisite's kind. With an existing output, `.PHONY: dir/../force`, and `output:: dir/../force`, the generated edge is scheduled but its runtime recipe group is skipped because the nonexistent lexical path is treated as an ordinary missing file. Direct execution recognizes the dependency through `lexical_output` and runs it. Preserve a lexical-to-canonical mapping or serialize the kind alongside each group input so aliases cannot suppress required builds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
